title: Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe first drive: Where tech and fun collide
gist: First-drive review of Mercedes-AMG's first battery-only AMG, the GT 4-Door Coupe, which uses three Yasa axial flux motors (up to 1,153 hp), an 800 V architecture and 600 kW DC fast charging. The reviewer judges it a track-capable technological triumph that largely overcomes the EV weight penalty, priced from $145,000 (GT 55) and $175,000 (GT 63).

themes.theme: Axial flux motors and in-house powertrain tech

insights.claim: The all-electric Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe uses three axial flux motors made by Yasa, which Mercedes acquired in 2021, delivering up to 1,153 hp (860 kW) peak and 711 hp nominal in the AMG GT 63 from motors only 79-89 mm wide.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Shows Mercedes' 2021 Yasa acquisition reaching production in a halo car, a differentiating vertically integrated EV motor technology.
insights.locator: Of the technology added to the

insights.claim: Mercedes' AMG.EA sports-car architecture coordinates power delivery across the three motors with active suspension, up to 6 degrees of rear-axle steering and active aerodynamics, which the reviewer says largely removes the battery-weight handling penalty of EVs.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Software-defined chassis control is becoming the key lever for premium EV performance differentiation.
insights.quote: the company has mostly reduced the battery-weight tax that mires EV performance

insights.claim: The AMG GT 4-Door Coupe moves to an 800 V system rated for up to 600 kW DC fast charging; in a demo a track car peaked at 637 kW, still drew 252 kW at 79% charge, and charged from 17% to 80% in about 10 minutes.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Sets a new charging-speed benchmark that raises the bar for charging infrastructure providers and competing premium EVs.

insights.claim: Mercedes cools the cylindrical cells of the 106 kWh pack with a non-conductive oil routed past connectors and cell centers, enabling both fast charging and repeated Boost-mode use, though it declines to disclose the oil chemistry or range targets.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Immersion-style thermal management is emerging as a proprietary performance edge; undisclosed range leaves an open question on efficiency.

insights.claim: The AMG GT 55 starts at $145,000 plus $1,550 destination and arrives by end of 2026, while the AMG GT 63 starts at $175,000 and arrives in early 2027.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Defines Mercedes' top-end EV price point and timing for the halo model's revenue contribution.
insights.locator: Kids love fun. Adults love fun.

insights.claim: The reviewer argues the car should end the perception that all EVs drive the same, using synthesized V8 sound with seat actuators and driver-adjustable Response/Agility/Traction dials to recreate an emotional performance-car experience.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Legacy luxury brands are betting on experiential differentiation to defend premium pricing as EV powertrains commoditize.
insights.quote: the electric coupe should squelch the “all EVs drive the same” discourse
insights.locator: Kids love fun. Adults love fun.
